# Syrtis v0.5.0

**Read this before updating: once v0.5.0 has run, going back to v0.4.1 or earlier empties your quota history.** Details below. There is no reason to go back, but if you install an older copy over this one, that is what happens.

## Quota history that no longer falls apart

The Quota lens learns how fast you spend each window from its own history. On Windows that history kept splitting: every time a sign-in refreshed its token, Syrtis started a new, empty history for the same account. On a real machine, one Claude account had been split into more than a dozen separate histories, and the window history card showed a single cycle while weeks of cycles sat where it could no longer reach them.

This release fixes it:

- **History now stays with you across token refreshes.** It is keyed to your subscription, not to the current sign-in token.
- **The pieces are merged back once, on the first run.** Cycles recorded before this update reappear in the window history card.
- **A damaged history file is repaired instead of freezing.** Previously one bad entry could stop every later reading from being saved.

This brings Windows' quota engine back in line with the macOS build, which had moved ahead.

**Two things change as a result:**

- **No going back.** The history file is upgraded to a new format the first time v0.5.0 saves to it. An older Syrtis cannot read that format; it sets the file aside and starts an empty one.
- **Claude, Copilot and Grok keep one history per computer**, not one per account. If you switch between two accounts of the same service on one Windows install, their quota history is shared. Codex and the Antigravity IDE still keep accounts apart. This matches the macOS build.

## Tabs for every subscription you have

The tab row used to list only tools with usage recorded on this computer. It now also lists services you are signed in to that only report a quota, such as **GitHub Copilot**, so their Quota lens is one click away. A service you are not signed in to does not get a tab.

**Antigravity's IDE and command-line tool now share one "Antigravity" tab**, since they draw on the same subscription. Your earlier tab order and hidden tabs carry over.

## Also in this release

- Hovering a row in the window history now breaks its tokens down into input, output, cache read, cache write and reasoning; hovering one of its models does the same for that model. Rows light up under the pointer like the other lists.
- The Session and Weekly tabs on the window card stay in a fixed order. Previously Weekly jumped to the front whenever no session was running.
- Syrtis now finds the Antigravity IDE's sign-in client in its Windows install. It needs that client to refresh an expired Antigravity sign-in, and it looked only in the macOS location before.
- An Antigravity or Codex sign-in file that exists but cannot be read is reported as unreadable, not as "not logged in".
- Grok's weekly allowance is read from the shared credit pool it is spent from, not from a single product's row, which could disagree with it.
